chapter: Later life, World's Fair and Ellington
title: Recent gigs: Harlem Blues and Jazz Band, Condon's and Red Blazer
summary: Hall describes the older musicians' band and other current groups.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah, uh-huh. And I got a lot of joy out of doing that. But the -- the thing you figure I'm interested in -- right now I've been working with Dr. Vollmer, who's a dentist, and he's got a group called the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band, and he takes them to Europe every year, and he drives the bus, and he books them and --
When did you last go on this?
Well, I haven't been on one of those trips, but I have worked with him locally.
Oh, you played with him here.
Uh-huh.
And the average age group of the guys is in their '70s.
So you're the youngest.
Clyde -- no --
(Laughter.)
Clyde Bernhardt --
The trombonist.

-- the trombonist, and George James, saxophonist, and Frank Williams, trumpet, and Tommy Benford has been playing, but he didn't play on this last engagement, so we had -- and what's his name, Sheldon Sullivan Garry.
He's the youngest.
Yeah, he's the youngest. I'm in between.
(Laughter.)
And --
Where do you play mostly?
Well, he gets gigs locally, schools and -- and recreational places and then books them all through Germany and Switzerland the one time of the year.
Uh-huh. Do you expect you'll be going to Europe with him this next trip?
Well, I've been substituting for Johnny Williams, so -- you know, it would be his availability whether I do that or not.
Uh-huh. Then you've also been working at Condon's some, haven't you?
I've been sitting in at Condon's and been working with Charles Wizan, Jazz Accorde.
Oh, yeah.
He's a French violinist.
Yeah, they sound like the Quintet of the Hot Club of France. Yeah, it's a nice little group. (inaudible) Mike Peters.
Yes, uh-huh. So we've been doing that at --
Red Blazer.

-- at the Red Blazer. Then I've worked at Red Blazer on Saturdays with Bob Cantwell, and we have a group called the Saturday Night Stompers, Dixieland type thing. So if between those something else comes up, it makes a week, a weak week.
(Laughter and recording interruption.)
